icon_url.basis: the firm's own site icon, normalized to the 256 PNG master and uploaded to the Icon Images bucket by scripts/fetch-investor-icon.ts (PRO-53 flow, re-run 2026-09-03 under the icon quality rules in scripts/utils/icon-normalize.ts). The source SVG is a single #303030 path with fill="none" on the root - a bare glyph on transparency, 84% transparent once rasterized - so the master carried no background and the near-black mark was invisible against the app's dark mode. history.value: Founded in 2000 by four ex-Weiss, Peck & Greer partners - Barry Eggers, Ravi Mhatre, Christopher Schaepe and Peter Nieh - Lightspeed grew from a Menlo Park enterprise-and-consumer early-stage shop into a multi-stage global platform investing from the US, Europe and Israel, with sister firms (not the same adviser) in India and China. Seed-to-IPO backer of Snap, Nutanix, MuleSoft, Affirm and Rubrik; since 2012 it has put over $5.5B into 165+ AI companies including Anthropic and Mistral AI, and closed its largest raise, $9B+, in December 2025.

investment_range.basis: Median: partner-anchored entry-round median $17,875,690 across 112 membership-verified base companies with priced Form D histories (31 entries anchored past pre-investor rounds, 0 unanchored), on the FINAL post-classification base (875 rows, full ledger coverage, PRO-66's second China sweep and 13 further identity merges applied 2026-09-03); published as $18M. p10 $3.0M, p25 $7.0M, p75 $35.0M, p90 $100.0M (scratch/verified-median.json). Stable across three populations: $17.25M interim (71 site-confirmed issuers, pre-base) / $17.50M at base checkpoint 2 (115 members, 931-row base) / $17.88M final (112 members, 875-row base). A round-size proxy for check size, fair for a high-ownership lead investor. | Lower limit: the $485,000 sole-investor Snapchat seed (May 2012, Jeremy Liew; Slate 2013-12, TechCrunch 2017-02-25) - a documented smallest-entry class, not a program floor. | Upper limit: the $13B Anthropic Series F (announced 2025-09-02, $183B post) which Lightspeed CO-LED with ICONIQ (lead) and Fidelity (anthropic.com/news/anthropic-raises-series-f-at-usd183b-post-money-valuation) - a co-led round figure, not a single-check claim; Lightspeed's own commitment reported ~$1B (The Tech Portal 2025-12-16). Dry-powder check: Opportunity III ($3.28B) at 10-15% single-position concentration supports $330-495M positions; the 2025 $1.25B single-asset vehicles plus Co-Investment Fund I ($601M) explain capacity above that

funds.basis: 15 funds, vintage 2016-2025, from the full Lightspeed* Form D issuer sweep over the local 2008q1-2026q2 bulk datasets plus live EDGAR full-text search for 2026q3 (51 own vehicles, 63 filings in sources/edgar/fund-formds.json). Where a fund filed a real sold amount it is asserted against the filing at build time (7 entries with accessions: XI, Select II, and the five December 2025 closes). The firm's modern filing style is an Indefinite offering with $0 sold at first filing and no amendment until close - so unlike Accel, a total-offering cross-check is structurally unavailable, and the 2020-2022 generations (XIII, Select IV, Opportunity I, XIV-A/B, Select V, Opportunity II) publish press sizes with the filings as existence corroboration. XII and Select III co-file one Form D; their split is S&P's read of the 2019 amendment and sums to the filed total exactly. Excluded from the list, with the treatment flagged: the SIV/SPV/access-vehicle trail (AI Renaissance, Ascent $1.14B GAV, Velocity, Platinum, Luminous VI-A/B, M2/M1-B, Affiliates X, Strategic Partners I, the SPV-* and *-Holdings series, LS Opportunities Access funds, LS Investments C - the ADV's one non-discretionary account, OYO/UDAAN deal vehicles, legacy VII/VIII trusts), the $1.25B of 2025 single-investor vehicles (press, no per-vehicle sizes), and the ~$600M August 2026 continuation vehicle (decisions.md #6: fund plumbing). Pre-2016 families (X + Select I, IX and earlier) predate the 10-year window. China I-IV + China Select I, India Partners I-V and the Faction funds are separate firms (decisions.md #2-4) and are excluded from the sweep file itself

flags.note: Single sworn number, both range ends: the one RIA covers all three desks (unlike Accel, no in-boundary ERA adds a second sworn figure). The FY2025 ADV predates the December 2025 closes (XV-A/B, Select VI final, Opportunity III final, Co-Invest I) and the 2026 vehicles (M2, Velocity, Platinum, AI Renaissance, INF/NH/SU Holdings, SPV-A4/A5/OB2), so current RAUM is higher. Press '>$40B globally' (Dec 2025) is below the sworn floor and is not published. The $32.1B non-US-person attribution is the ADV's own figure and does not contradict the US-led firm reading (fund vehicles are largely Cayman/Delaware partnerships with global LPs).

Filing-style caveat: Indefinite offerings with $0 sold at first filing mean six of the fifteen sizes rest on press alone (XIII, Select IV, Opportunity I, XIV-A/B, Select V, Opportunity II - all Debevoise-confirmed closes). XIV-A/B is published as one entry at the announced $1.98B because the sleeve split is undisclosed. XII/Select III sizes are S&P's split of a joint filing (sums to the filed $2,113.8M exactly); Select III's July 2018 close was $1.05B before the 2019 $311.8M additional closing. Where press and filing disagree the filed amount is published (Select VI $1.745B vs press $1.8B; XV-A $977.7M vs $980M; XV-B $1,194.9M vs $1.2B; Co-Invest I $601.3M vs $600M).

Median tracked the base through both shifts and stayed within $650K: $17.25M pre-base / $17.50M at the 931-row checkpoint / $17.88M on the final 875-row base (published $18M, nearest million; the earlier renders showed $17M). Priced Form D rounds only; SAFE and 4(a)(2) rounds do not file, so the small end is under-sampled, and the partner-anchored first filing is a ceiling on entry recency (31 of 112 entries anchored past pre-investor rounds).
